Class MarkdownElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<MarkdownElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.markdown.MarkdownElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class MarkdownElement extends StyledElement<MarkdownElement>
Toolkit DSL element rendering CommonMark + GFM markdown via MarkdownView. Inherits the standard StyledElement fluent API (color, modifiers, layout constraints, CSS classes) and adds markdown-specific options.

CSS rules attached to MarkdownElement (or any user-supplied type/id/class) flow through to MarkdownView, so the same heading-1-color, link-color, blockquote-prefix and so on documented on MarkdownView apply here.

Example: 

import static dev.tamboui.toolkit.Toolkit.*;
import static dev.tamboui.toolkit.markdown.MarkdownElement.markdown;

panel("README",
    markdown(readme).overflow(Overflow.WRAP_WORD).fill()
).rounded();

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size

      protected void renderContent(Frame frame, Rect area, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from class: StyledElement
      Renders the content of this element.

      Subclasses implement this method to perform their specific rendering. The current style (CSS + inline, merged with parent styles) is available via RenderContext.currentStyle().
